exam.title: Numerical Mathematics - Expert Exam
exam.subtitle: Algorithms, Approximation and Error Analysis
exam.instructions: Complete all tasks thoroughly. Specify algorithms explicitly and perform error analyses. Permitted aids: non-programmable calculator.

exercises.title: Newton's Method with Convergence Analysis
exercises.description:
Given the function f(x) = x³ - 2x - 5.

a) Show that f has a root in the interval [2, 3].
b) Perform three iterations of Newton's method with starting value x₀ = 2.5.
c) Estimate the absolute error after the third iteration.
d) Determine the convergence order of Newton's method for this problem.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a) - Existence of root
f(2) = 2³ - 2·2 - 5 = 8 - 4 - 5 = -1 < 0
f(3) = 3³ - 2·3 - 5 = 27 - 6 - 5 = 16 > 0
Since f is continuous and f(2) < 0 < f(3), by the intermediate value theorem there exists at least one root in [2,3].

Step 2: Prepare Newton's method
f(x) = x³ - 2x - 5
f'(x) = 3x² - 2
Newton iteration: $x_{n+1} = x_n - \frac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)} = x_n - \frac{x_n³ - 2x_n - 5}{3x_n² - 2}$

Step 5: Part c) - Error estimation
For Newton's method with sufficiently good approximation:
$|x_{n+1} - x*| ≤ \frac{M}{2m} |x_n - x*|²$
where M = max|f''(x)| and m = min|f'(x)| in the relevant range.
f''(x) = 6x, so f''(2.094) ≈ 12.564
Estimate: $|x₃ - x*| ≤ \frac{12.564}{2·11.17} |x₂ - x*|² ≈ 0.56|x₂ - x*|²$

Step 6: Part d) - Convergence order
Newton's method has quadratic convergence for simple roots.
Since f'(x*) = 3(x*)² - 2 ≠ 0 for the root x* ≈ 2.094, the convergence order is p = 2.
This means: $|x_{n+1} - x*| = O(|x_n - x*|²)$ for n → ∞.

exercises.title: Lagrange Interpolation with Error Analysis
exercises.description:
Given the interpolation points and function values:
(x₀, y₀) = (0, 1), (x₁, y₁) = (1, 2), (x₂, y₂) = (2, 5), (x₃, y₃) = (3, 10)

a) Determine the Lagrange interpolation polynomial p₃(x).
b) Estimate the interpolation error for f(x) = x² + 1 at point x = 1.5.
c) Calculate the divided differences and the Newton interpolation polynomial.
solutionSteps:
Step 2: Lagrange interpolation polynomial
p₃(x) = y₀L₀(x) + y₁L₁(x) + y₂L₂(x) + y₃L₃(x)
= 1·L₀(x) + 2·L₁(x) + 5·L₂(x) + 10·L₃(x)
After expansion and simplification:
p₃(x) = x² + 1

Step 3: Part b) - Error analysis
Since f(x) = x² + 1 and p₃(x) = x² + 1 agree, the interpolation error is exactly zero.
General error formula: $|f(x) - p_n(x)| ≤ \frac{M_{n+1}}{(n+1)!} |ω(x)|$
where ω(x) = ∏(x - x_i) and M_{n+1} = max|f^{(n+1)}(ξ)|
For f(x) = x² + 1: f'''(x) = 0, therefore the error is exactly zero.

Step 4: Part c) - Divided differences scheme
f[x₀] = f(0) = 1
f[x₁] = f(1) = 2
f[x₀,x₁] = (f[x₁] - f[x₀])/(x₁ - x₀) = (2-1)/(1-0) = 1
f[x₁,x₂] = (f[x₂] - f[x₁])/(x₂ - x₁) = (5-2)/(2-1) = 3
f[x₂,x₃] = (f[x₃] - f[x₂])/(x₃ - x₂) = (10-5)/(3-2) = 5

Step 5: Higher order divided differences
f[x₀,x₁,x₂] = (f[x₁,x₂] - f[x₀,x₁])/(x₂ - x₀) = (3-1)/(2-0) = 1
f[x₁,x₂,x₃] = (f[x₂,x₃] - f[x₁,x₂])/(x₃ - x₁) = (5-3)/(3-1) = 1
f[x₀,x₁,x₂,x₃] = (f[x₁,x₂,x₃] - f[x₀,x₁,x₂])/(x₃ - x₀) = (1-1)/(3-0) = 0

Step 6: Newton interpolation polynomial
p₃(x) = f[x₀] + f[x₀,x₁](x-x₀) + f[x₀,x₁,x₂](x-x₀)(x-x₁) + f[x₀,x₁,x₂,x₃](x-x₀)(x-x₁)(x-x₂)
= 1 + 1·x + 1·x(x-1) + 0·x(x-1)(x-2)
= 1 + x + x² - x = x² + 1
The Newton polynomial agrees with the Lagrange polynomial.

exercises.title: Composite Quadrature Rules
exercises.description:
Approximate the integral $I = \int_0^2 e^{-x^2} dx$ with n = 4 subintervals.

a) Use the composite trapezoidal rule.
b) Use the composite Simpson's rule.
c) Estimate the errors of both methods.
d) Compare the results with the exact value I ≈ 0.8820813908.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Preparation - Support points
Step size: h = (b-a)/n = (2-0)/4 = 0.5
Support points: x₀ = 0, x₁ = 0.5, x₂ = 1.0, x₃ = 1.5, x₄ = 2.0
Function values:
f(0) = e⁰ = 1
f(0.5) = e^{-0.25} ≈ 0.7788
f(1.0) = e^{-1} ≈ 0.3679
f(1.5) = e^{-2.25} ≈ 0.1054
f(2.0) = e^{-4} ≈ 0.0183

Step 4: Part c) - Error estimation trapezoidal rule
Trapezoidal rule error: $|E_T| ≤ \frac{(b-a)h^2}{12} \max_{x \in [a,b]} |f''(x)|$
f(x) = e^{-x²}, f'(x) = -2xe^{-x²}, f''(x) = (4x² - 2)e^{-x²}
f''(x) = 0 for x² = 1/2, so x = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707
Maximum of |f''(x)| on [0,2]: |f''(0)| = 2
|E_T| ≤ (2·(0.5)²·2)/12 = 1/12 ≈ 0.0833

Step 5: Error estimation Simpson's rule
Simpson's rule error: $|E_S| ≤ \frac{(b-a)h^4}{180} \max_{x \in [a,b]} |f^{(4)}(x)|$
After calculating the fourth derivative (complex):
$|E_S| ≤ \frac{2·(0.5)^4·M_4}{180}$ where M₄ ≈ 12 (estimated)
|E_S| ≤ (2·0.0625·12)/180 ≈ 0.0083

Step 6: Part d) - Comparison with exact value
Exact value: I ≈ 0.8820813908
Trapezoidal rule: T₄ ≈ 0.8806, Error ≈ |0.8821 - 0.8806| ≈ 0.0015
Simpson's rule: S₄ ≈ 0.8818, Error ≈ |0.8821 - 0.8818| ≈ 0.0003
Simpson's rule is significantly more accurate since it has order O(h⁴) compared to O(h²) for the trapezoidal rule.
The theoretical error bounds are conservative; the actual errors are smaller.

exercises.title: LU Decomposition with Pivoting
exercises.description:
Solve the linear system Ax = b with
$A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & 3 \\ 8 & 7 & 9 \end{pmatrix}, \quad b = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 10 \\ 24 \end{pmatrix}$

a) Perform LU decomposition without pivoting.
b) Solve the systems Ly = b and Ux = y.
c) Calculate the condition number κ∞(A) = ||A||∞ · ||A⁻¹||∞.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Part a) - Prepare LU decomposition
We decompose A = LU with L lower triangular matrix (diagonal = 1) and U upper triangular matrix.
Starting system:
$A^{(0)} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & 3 \\ 8 & 7 & 9 \end{pmatrix}$

Step 2: First elimination (column 1)
Multipliers: l₂₁ = a₂₁/a₁₁ = 4/2 = 2, l₃₁ = a₃₁/a₁₁ = 8/2 = 4
Row 2 new: (4,3,3) - 2·(2,1,1) = (0,1,1)
Row 3 new: (8,7,9) - 4·(2,1,1) = (0,3,5)
$A^{(1)} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 5 \end{pmatrix}$

Step 3: Second elimination (column 2)
Multiplier: l₃₂ = a₃₂⁽¹⁾/a₂₂⁽¹⁾ = 3/1 = 3
Row 3 new: (0,3,5) - 3·(0,1,1) = (0,0,2)
$U = A^{(2)} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$

Step 4: Construct L matrix
$L = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ l_{21} & 1 & 0 \\ l_{31} & l_{32} & 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
Verification: LU should yield A (can be checked).

Step 5: Part b) - Solve auxiliary systems
First solve Ly = b:
$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ y_3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 10 \\ 24 \end{pmatrix}$
Forward substitution:
y₁ = 4
y₂ = 10 - 2y₁ = 10 - 8 = 2
y₃ = 24 - 4y₁ - 3y₂ = 24 - 16 - 6 = 2

Step 6: Then solve Ux = y
$\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$
Backward substitution:
x₃ = 2/2 = 1
x₂ = 2 - 1·x₃ = 2 - 1 = 1
x₁ = (4 - 1·x₂ - 1·x₃)/2 = (4 - 1 - 1)/2 = 1
Solution: x = (1, 1, 1)ᵀ

Step 7: Part c) - Calculate condition number
||A||∞ = max of row sums = max{4, 10, 24} = 24
For A⁻¹ (calculation with Gauss-Jordan or cofactors):
$A^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1/2 & 0 \\ -6 & 5 & -1 \\ 2 & -3/2 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$
||A⁻¹||∞ = max{0.5, 12, 6.5} = 12
κ∞(A) = ||A||∞ · ||A⁻¹||∞ = 24 · 12 = 288
The matrix is moderately conditioned.

exercises.title: Runge-Kutta Method
exercises.description:
Solve the initial value problem y' = -2y + x, y(0) = 1 numerically in the interval [0, 1] with step size h = 0.2.

a) Apply the classical 4th-order Runge-Kutta method.
b) Compare with the exact solution y(x) = (x-1)/2 + 3e^{-2x}/2.
c) Analyze the stability of the method for this problem.
solutionSteps:
Step 1: Prepare 4th-order Runge-Kutta
Given: y' = f(x,y) = -2y + x, y(0) = 1, h = 0.2
RK4 formulas:
k₁ = hf(xₙ, yₙ)
k₂ = hf(xₙ + h/2, yₙ + k₁/2)
k₃ = hf(xₙ + h/2, yₙ + k₂/2)
k₄ = hf(xₙ + h, yₙ + k₃)
yₙ₊₁ = yₙ + (k₁ + 2k₂ + 2k₃ + k₄)/6

Step 3: Further iterations
Second iteration (x₁ = 0.2, y₁ ≈ 0.6893):
Analogous calculations lead to y₂ ≈ 0.5238
Third iteration (x₂ = 0.4, y₂ ≈ 0.5238):
y₃ ≈ 0.4493
Fourth iteration (x₃ = 0.6, y₃ ≈ 0.4493):
y₄ ≈ 0.4187
Fifth iteration (x₄ = 0.8, y₄ ≈ 0.4187):
y₅ ≈ 0.4184

Step 5: Error analysis
Error at x = 0.2: |0.6893 - 0.6070| ≈ 0.0823
Error at x = 0.4: |0.5238 - 0.4493| ≈ 0.0745
The errors are reasonably large for RK4 with h = 0.2.
Global error of RK4: O(h⁴), local error: O(h⁵)

Step 6: Part c) - Stability analysis
For the model equation y' = λy with λ = -2, the stability region is relevant.
RK4 stability condition: |1 + hλ + (hλ)²/2 + (hλ)³/6 + (hλ)⁴/24| < 1
With hλ = 0.2·(-2) = -0.4:
|1 - 0.4 + 0.08 - 0.0107 + 0.0007| = |0.6700| < 1
The method is stable for this step size.
Critical step size for absolute stability: h < 2.785/|λ| = 1.39
